graph.name: 7. Let a second model polish the narration
graph.description:
Use a second model pass to polish narration while preserving dialogue and an exact place name.

What you'll learn:
• Preparation happens before the reply is written; response processing works on the draft afterward.
• Revise Draft requests an edited draft. Editable scope limits the kind of text it may change, and Protected literals lists wording that must stay exact.

Before you start:
• Use a practice SillyTavern chat where you can try things freely. Open this example, then turn on Enable Lattice before sending a message. Your usual SillyTavern connection writes the reply.
• Choose a working connection for Revise Draft · narration pass, the Prose job. Use a practice scene where North Harbor and dialogue can appear.

Steps:
1. Select Text and read its instruction about concrete sounds and movement. Follow it through Compose into Generate Reply.guidance; this part shapes the first draft.
2. Select Revise Draft · narration pass. In Details, check Editable scope is narration and Protected literals contains North Harbor. Read Instructions to see the requested polish.
3. Choose Active SillyTavern model or another configured connection in the revision box’s connection bar. This extra pass can use the same model as the main reply.
4. Send “At North Harbor, Rowan says, ‘The lighthouse is dark.’ Describe the sounds around us.” After it finishes, preview Generate Reply.draft to read the first version.
5. Preview Revise Draft.out and compare it with that first version. Look for tighter narration, unchanged dialogue, and North Harbor spelled exactly the same.
6. Follow the revised draft’s wire into Review / Publish. The version awaiting review is the polished draft, rather than a separate disconnected piece of text.
7. Finish at Review / Publish. Open its Host result in Preview, then choose Apply reviewed candidate to keep the proposed version or Reject candidate to discard it. Previewing an output does not make that choice for you.

Checkpoints:
Revise Draft · narration pass → out: The revised draft may improve narration; dialogue and the protected words North Harbor remain unchanged.

Try this:
Change Editable scope to dialogue for a separate practice run.
The editable region changes. Compare the drafts to check that narration is preserved instead.

If something is different:
The model tries to change protected wording or text outside the chosen scope.: Validation reports the problem rather than silently accepting the prohibited edit.
You only preview an intermediate revision.: Preview lets you compare text. Keeping a final version still goes through Review / Publish.

Model requests: At most 1 extra Revise Draft request after 1 normal SillyTavern reply. A draft with no editable narration needs no revision request.

direction.title: Text
direction.text: Describe the scene through concrete sounds and movement; preserve dialogue and player agency.

polish.title: Revise Draft
polish.instructions: Tighten repetition and sentence rhythm. Preserve facts, chronology, all dialogue and North Harbor exactly.
